summary: This change passes. It adds one conditional paragraph to the change producer prompt (`crates/athena-cap-change/prompts/producer.md`). When a job's files are under `studies/`, the producer must open each claim id cited by a new or reworded statement and check that the claim says what the sentence says, including who does the action. It must also list each changed statement with its claim text in the change description, and either add a sourced claim or drop any statement no claim supports. The changelog may never say claims support a wording unless they do. The rule is written up for a stranger in `docs/conventions/study-claim-support.md`, marked prose-only and recorded in `CHANGELOG.md`. Targeting the change prompt is right: the evidence snapshot shows that the five earlier jobs where the verifier found unsupported study statements all ran under the change capability. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and test checks passed, and I ran the budget tests myself: 7 passed, with the producer prompt at 1043 of 1200 tokens. There are three minor findings: (1) `docs/system-facts.md` is edited outside the deliverables list, but a budget test requires that edit; (2) the new spec.toml text sits under OLY-B-A7-03, though OLY-B-JDG-03 or OLY-B-S5-01 fits better; (3) the convention doc says the verifier checks the rule, but no verifier prompt tells it to. There is also one nit: the changelog entry leaves out the changelog-honesty part of the rule.
